articles.title: 'Trump what is going on with you?' President's biggest fans panic as he takes Dem's bait
articles.description: President Donald Trump's own supporters are begging him to explain himself after he shared a Democrat's pitch for government-guaranteed healthcare with his name on it. On Saturday, Trump reposted to Truth Social a message from Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D), without comment. In the post, El-Sayed showed off mock-ups of a gold "TrumpCare" insurance card bearing the president's signature. "This is a message for @realDonaldTrump," El-Sayed had written on X. "Donald, this is on the table. Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave." El-Sayed, a physician who campaigned on Medicare for All, has openly appealed to Trump's ego to sell the idea, saying the program could make him "the most popular president in the history of America." Trump's repost suggested the pitch may be landing. The same day, he told Fox News he might be open to working with Democrats on healthcare. His base was not on board. "President Trump what is going on with you?" wrote a Truth Social user named Catherine Turbitt Shiver, whose handle is @Trumpgirl452024. Her bio reads "TRUMP WON!! THEY CHEATED!!" and includes "WWG1WGA," a QAnon slogan. Her pinned post, from Election Day 2024, says, "I personally endorse @realDonaldTrump." "Why would you agree with this guy? Nobody wants Medicare for everybody. I'm on Medicare at f---ing sucks," she continued. "Why would you even post anything from this guy?" She went on to call El-Sayed "a socialist" and "a radical Muslim." Another Florida user, who goes by Lady Ferrum Quartz and whose bio warns that she blocks "anyone who spews hate at President Trump," was just as blunt. "I don't trust that El Sayed one bit," she wrote. "He just wants more free healthcare for more foreigners and illegal immigrants. Medicare for all is bulls---. Putting the great name of Trump on it won't change that." A Texas user named Joseph, whose profile banner shows Trump's face carved into Mount Rushmore and whose pinned post argues against impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, called the plan "just government run healthcare with a fancy name." "Abdul El-Sayed is trying to sell President Trump a gold card that gives free healthcare from cradle to grave," he wrote. "Americans already know what that costs and who pays for it." Mike Neely, who describes himself as a retired Navy officer and whose profile reshares pro-Trump content, added that, "Democrats don't know the term. For them, the cradle is a grave." An account whose display name includes the hashtag "#IStandWithTrump" responded with a meme calling El-Sayed "an arrogant a--hole with the personality of a psychopath." Another user called him a "little commie" and fumed about him addressing the president as "Donald." Many of the more than 1,400 replies went further. Some attacked El-Sayed's Muslim faith. One account insisted, without basis, that the senator-elect is "illegitimate" and "must not be sworn in." The backlash echoed criticism from right-wing activist Laura Loomer, who blasted the repost as an endorsement of "socialized healthcare" and "Obama Care with President Trump's name on it." She also suggested Trump may not have known it was posted to his account. Trump spent years vowing to repeal and replace the Affordable Care Act. His administration has said it is preparing its own healthcare plan, and Vice President JD Vance said this week that the White House wants to work with Democrats to fix a "broken" system. El-Sayed won Michigan's open Senate seat in this month's midterms and will be sworn in in January. Asked about Trump's repost, he told Fox 2 Detroit, "I'm happy to chat."
